text: When you wake up in the morning, tell yourself: the people I deal with today will be meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest, jealous, and surly. But I have seen the beauty of good, and the ugliness of evil, and have recognized that the wrongdoer has a nature related to my own.

Do not waste what remains of your life in speculating about your neighbors, unless it is for mutual benefit. Focus your attention on what you do, and remember that your purpose is to be a good person.
Do not be disturbed by the impressions that crowd your mind. Master them through reflection, and occupy yourself with what is in your power — the use you make of your perceptions.
You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do, say, and think.
At every moment, keep a firm hold on your purpose. Decide what kind of person you want to be, and do the work to become it.
If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself but to your estimate of it. You have the power to revoke it at any moment.
Do not be ashamed to seek help. You must carry out the task before you like a soldier storming a wall. What if you are lame and cannot climb alone? Ask a comrade to help you.
Nothing is worth doing pointlessly. To what purpose, then, do you act? That is the question you must ask yourself.

People try to get away from it all — to the country, to the beach, to the mountains. You always wish that you could too. But that is foolish. You can get away from it anytime you like by going within.
Today I escaped from anxiety. Or no, I discarded it, because it was within me, in my own perceptions — not outside.
Choose not to be harmed — and you will not feel harmed. Do not feel harmed — and you have not been.
The things you think about determine the quality of your mind. Your soul takes on the color of your thoughts.
At dawn, when you have trouble getting out of bed, say to yourself: I have to go to work — as a human being. What do I have to complain of, if I am going to do what I was born for?
Just as nature takes every obstacle, every impediment, and works it around, turns it to its purposes — so a rational being can turn every setback into raw material for their purpose.
The mind adapts and converts to its own purposes the obstacle to our acting. The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
You are a small soul carrying around a corpse, as Epictetus said.
The best revenge is to be unlike the one who performed the injury.
The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts. Take care that you do not entertain notions unfit for virtue.
The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority but to avoid being in the ranks of the insane.
Do not act as if you had ten thousand years to throw away. Death stands at your elbow. Be good for something while you live.
Does anyone do wrong? It is to themselves that they do harm. Has something happened to you? It is well. Everything that happens has always happened, and will happen again.
Nowhere you can go is more peaceful — more free of interruptions — than your own soul.
Do not let the future disturb you. You will meet it, if you have to, with the same weapons of reason which today arm you against the present.
Remember that to change your mind and to follow someone who corrects your error is as consistent with freedom as it is to persist in your error.
Let no act be done without purpose. Let your actions be just and consistent with the principle of doing good.
You have power over your mind — not over external events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
Waste no more time arguing what a good person should be. Be one.
The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts. Dye it, then, with thoughts of justice, self-control, courage, and freedom.
Despise not death, but welcome it. It too is according to nature. To fear death is to fear the loss of sensation, or another kind of sensation.
The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing. Stand ready to meet the unexpected.
If someone can prove me wrong and show me my mistake in any thought or action, I shall gladly change. I seek the truth, which never harmed anyone. The harm is to persist in self-deception.
Everything is only for a day. The one who died and the one who mourns them — they are both only for a day.
Like the sand, so is everything that has happened. And like the sand, so is everything that will happen. Nothing is new under the sun.
The soul should be ready to part from the body at any moment. This readiness comes from inner conviction, not from blind resistance.
If someone is able to show me that what I think or do is not right, I will gladly change. It is the truth I seek, and the truth never harmed anyone.
Do not let the force of the impression carry you away. Say to it: wait for me a little while, let me see what you are and what you represent. Let me put you to the test.
The only thing that is your own is the present moment. The past is gone, the future unknown. Life is short. Make the most of this moment.
If you seek tranquility, do less. Or rather, do what is essential. This brings the double satisfaction of doing less and doing it better.
